sentences.text: Flamingos aren't born pink. Their chicks start out with white-gray feathers. So who upgrades them to pink?
The answer is on the menu. Flamingos get their pink color from pigments in their food.
Those pigments are called carotenoids. Plants make them, and they're also found in microscopic algae eaten by brine shrimp.
When flamingos eat foods like algae and brine shrimp, their bodies process those pigments, turning their feathers pink.
And their dining technique is unusual. A feeding flamingo puts its head upside down in the water and sweeps its bill side to side.
Its tongue pumps water through the bill. Comb-like plates let the water out while trapping food inside.
So, is a flamingo making a fashion statement... or just wearing its lunch receipt?
